newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 9.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The South African Reserve Bank's gold and foreign exchange reserves ended last year on a dismal note, dropping more than 629 million rand in December to 10.3 billion rand in a final reminder that the country was the black sheep of emerging market economies last year.

- Commuter rail service provider Metro Rail will be set up as a separate division of Transnet in the next few months, paving the way for government to introduce competition into the sector by next year.

- Government's standing advisory committee on company law is likely to recommend that nominee companies -- which control more than a third of the Johannesburg Stock Exchange's market capitalisation -- should be foreced to name shareholders holding significant stakes in the firms, sources say.
- The South African revenue service is preparing to visit taxpayers who fail to apply for the new tax amnesty.
- More than one billion rand of corporate bonds will be launched next month by the Infrastructure Finance Corp (Inca), launched in October, Johan Kruger, Inca's managing director said.

- The Reserve Bank's holding of gross gold and foreign exchange reserves dropped by almost 630 million rand to 10.3 billion rand in December, wiping out nearly all of the build-up of reserves over the previous two months.
- South Africa's gold share bloodbath of the past ten days has been indiscriminate with sellers unaccountably hitting the high graders as well as the marginals.
- Signs of light at the end of South Africa's tunnel of high interest rates appeared as rates in the money market edged down.

- Associated Insurance Brokers and Ragi Moonsamy, a well-known black insurance broker, have established joint-venture Associated Insurance Brokers Africa to help small brokers compete with big broking houses.

- The Post Office has cold comfort for people who have complained about non-delivery of overseas Christmas mail or those who claim that a massive backlog developed in the province of Gauteng over the festive season.
- Police are still looking for the armed gang who broke into a Malvern home, tied up the family and repeatedly raped two teenage cousins.
